reviews.text:
Overall this is an extremely zippy dark comedy that pays just enough attention to the tragedy
of its antiheroine without ever taking itself too seriously.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: Anchored by Stone's hilarious and engaged performance, Disney has finally created a worthwhile entry in its live-action formula.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: The feature film in question is a journey of self-knowledge of the young Estella who becomes Cruella, who manages to build the status of the character who will define herself as “brilliant, evil and crazy”...
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: Whether or not this intensely directed style works here, it’s a welcomed change from the recent corporate-productional feel of the most recent crop of Disney films.
reviews.author: Joshua Polanski

reviews.text: If only Cruella were just casually lazy, it could idly coast from one ear to the next without leaving much of a memory. But it’s almost alarming how malicious and toxic the whole thing feels.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: Set in the emerging punk scene of 1970s London, the Craig Gillespie-directed prequel of the iconic Cruella De Vil is the perfect film to bring people back to the theater.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: As beautifully shot, written and acted as it is full of personality and style, Disney’s Cruella is a graphic novel-worthy origin story that beautifully captures its protagonist’s dichotomy.
reviews.author: Serena Seghedoni

reviews.text: Boasting terrific lead performances and incredible costume design, Cruella is undeniably one of the better live action stories Disney has given us. However, the pacing issues and shoddy first half stop this from reaching true greatness.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: A creative, stylish, & snappy Disney Live Action Film yet. A must see in theaters for the fascinating directing & INCREDIBLE performance from EMMA STONE
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: An incredibly captivating origin(al) story about one of Disney's classic villains. Emma Stone delivers an award-worthy display, interpreting two personalities in impressive fashion, stealing the spotlight from the other outstanding interpretations.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Ultimately, it’s impossible to deny that Cruella is fun. Stone is clearly enjoying being eccentric as she flounces around London in her outlandish costumes, bringing mayhem wherever she goes.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Cruella doesn’t just retell an old story. It creates a lavish comic-book villain-style origin that opens up the film to an even larger audience.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Cruella manages to overcome its inherent flaws with tremendous style and just enough of a flirtation with tearing down the Disney machinery to make it feel edgier than it actually is.
reviews.author: Tom Fitzgerald and Lorenzo Marquez

reviews.text: Cruella is pure, perfect big studio escapism. It’s a witty, suspenseful, ultra-cool, killer Disney live-action triumph.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: A stylish new spin to an iconic character.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Cruella is absolute trashy cinema, but it certainly is my kind of trash. Basically, The Devil Wears Prada for the queer crowd who loves to stan a messy villain.
reviews.author: Jessie Gender

reviews.text: Cruella doesn't really feel like a Disney movie, and I truly mean that as a compliment. It's much darker than one might expect but never takes itself too seriously.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: The best way to enjoy and even understand Cruella is to see it as a punk opera, in which what moves the needle are not so much the musical segments but the dresses on display.
reviews.author: Agustín Acevedo Kanopa

reviews.text: A kind of family friendly Joker  a retro tale of a misfit searching for identity, before giving into the madness. Did we need to know how Cruella became such a devil? Probably not. Then again, darlings, it was a lot of fun.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Despite a strong effort from Emma Stone, Cruella does little to justify meaning in a story that turns irredeemable Disney villains into well-meaning, underdog antiheroes.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: If there is one thing this movie did best in terms of remaking 101 Dalmatians, its perfectly capturing Cruellas insanity, not just for the character herself, but for the entire picture.
reviews.author: Mat Brunet

reviews.text: It is incredibly easy to get lost within Cruella's world and have a fun time with the characters and camp that exist within the film's runtime.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: This soundtrack was wild...Stone was good, but not fantastic.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: Unnecessary but still fun...
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: Once the plot's major twist is unveiled, we're watching a duel between Emma Stone as Estella and Emma Thompson as the Baroness, and the two divas revel in their roles, chewing scenery and striking dramatic poses and just being super fabulous.
reviews.author: Popmatters Staff

reviews.text: The two female leads here are great. The two Emmas.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: Gillespie and his team have delivered audiences a suitably wicked and well-acted backstory for one of Disney's greatest villains.
reviews.author: Emma Badame

reviews.text: It has trouble making the ride a smooth one back to 1961's One Hundred and One Dalmatians.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The film's stylish nature, dedication to period accurateness, breathtaking costume design, and deliberate musical touches, not to mention a truly game cast puts this one in the surprisingly great category that neither of us can hate.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Cruella herself would find the movie dull and obvious, a wannabe punk decked out in Hot Topic.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: A surprisingly stylish, prickly and fun backstory for an already-iconic character.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Bizarre, dumb, busy, far too long, and ugly to look at. But at least the two leads are having a good time staring each other down while dad's punk mix plays in the background.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: This isn't quite the revelation that 2014's Maleficent was, but it's entertaining and exquisitely designed.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: Filmmaker Craig Gillespie creates a great sense of mood and tone, which can be defined as bold, elegant and intoxicating.
reviews.author: Tatat Bunnag

reviews.text: What could've been a gripping narrative about a woman gradually giving in to her darker impulses is undercut by its need to tie into an existing family friendly Disney property.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: The sexiest, most flagrantly fabulous film ever to emanate from Disney.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: This origin story of Disney's enigmatic supervillain is designed to entertain, even if you're not a fan or a follower of this famed franchise.
reviews.author: Ronak Kotecha

reviews.text: I like both Stone and Thompson in the film-they play off each other well. A psychological workup of the key characters would be interesting.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: Cruella has the same problem as Game of Thrones' final season. [... It] needed Daenerys to become the antagonist. [Though] Cruella's heel turn isn't as horrible, it's certainly not believable.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: An overblown and unnecessary waste of $200 million, Disney's Cruella encapsulates everything that is wrong with modern studio moviemaking and the IP-driven approach that the Mouse House is responsible for cultivating.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Cruella makes the best of what was always going to be a tough assignment; it's far from the disaster some may have been anticipating, but aside from the production design, it never reaches any particularly dizzying heights.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: The visual pomp of our anti-heroine is unveiled with a great sense of mischievous fun by Gillespie.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Superb production & costume design. Wouldn't be surprised to see any of these costumes be the new Halloween must-haves. Love the soundtrack, performances & easily a rewatchable movie.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Visually striking, fashionably astute and all-embracingly entertaining, this dynamic production stands as one of the finest pieces of mainstream filmmaking of the year so far.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Emma Stone is undoubtedly the best part about this movie.
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: A subversive 'mean girl' fairytale turned into a lavish spectacle that needed sharper writing and a clear sense of why this origin story is needed in the first place
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: Humanizing Cruella De Vil is not an easy task... Much of the credit goes to Emma Stone. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Valencia

reviews.text: Pieces of the plot fall out now and then, but enough good bites remain to savor.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: The duality is in fact, the essence of the film, which aims to give its anti-heroine a relatable rationale for her provocations while still keeping her de-vil-ish. With fiendish performances and striking production, they more than succeed.
reviews.author: Lina Lecaro

reviews.text: While Emma Stone approaches her role with some relish, she just isn't convincing as, well, a bitch.
reviews.author: Gabrielle Marceau

reviews.text: 'Curella' is wicked, stylish fun.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Cruella de Vil has incredible style and evil minions at her beck and call. She is certainly a feminist, she's all-Disney, and if she turns out to be more anti-heroine than heroine, well, that's part of the fun.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: Cruella is pure putrid poison, a camped-up extravaganza disguised as harmless kiddie crud. I guess you could say I didn't much care for it.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: The way [Emma Stone] elevates things in Cruella, taking what is a mediocre, fairly formulaic script and making it sing... isn't something a lot of people can do, and it's thrilling to watch.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: The only thing casual about the Baroness is her cruelty, and Thompson effortlessly plays it to the hilt.
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: A visually sumptuous, thematically ambitious, messy bitch of a film.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: Look, I'm not saying it makes sense, but Cruella kinda rocks. It has no business being this fun, but a delightful surprise for sure.
reviews.author: Amanda the Jedi

reviews.text: Cruella works best when it's not beholden to a bigger franchise, and instead offers glimpses of a far more exciting non-Dalmatian-related movie.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: In the wake of redundant 'reworks', the supremely entertaining Cruella is far from a dog's dinner, establishing its own thrilling identity with aplomb.
reviews.author: Darryl Griffiths

reviews.text: Times change and Disney (once the most conservative studio in Hollywood) adapts to this era of openings and diversities. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: I was hesitant about this origin story, but there is no need to worry, because "Cruella" is absolutely spectacular. Writers Dana Fox and Tony McNamara provide a refreshing spin on the character we love to hate.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: Cruella makes a splash, all right, for all the wrong reasons. It's not quite as bad as the Ms. De Vil inside my head claims, but it's still very much an overinflated miss.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Hugely disappointing.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: Very enjoyable if rather "fur coat and no knickers". Despite the noise, barbs and general gorgeousness, it feels empty, devoid even of wickedness.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: Emma Thompson is fantastic in this. The Baroness is a withering, mirror dimension Miss Money-Sterling, and is a crucial factor in Cruella's success.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: The most fun installment in the franchise.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The sheer volume of outfits worn by Stone and the rest of the cast, is matched only by the level of detail on each.
reviews.author: Damian Levy

reviews.text: The result is the complete mangling of one of the greatest Disney villains of all time.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Stylish and entertaining, but could probably stand to lose 15 minutes.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: These clothes are the boldest element of a movie that otherwise wears its supposed punk-rock influences like a kid discovering Hot Topic for the first time.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: It would have been deadly for a movie as fashion-centred as this to not deliver on costume design, but thankfully, the outfits worn by both Emmas are, as they say, something else.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Does Satan himself have an origin story that makes his evil understandable, even excusable? The ending of Cruella suggests as much.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: Cruella is a stylish and engaging romp with strong performances and exceptional design.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: From the moment you agree to leave the measured, logical mechanics of our world behind and spend a couple of hours in Cruella's mind instead, you're in for one hell of a ride
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: Cruella does what all bad prequels do, answering questions no one is asking.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Poor craftsmanship and a clumsy script undermine Disney's latest origin story.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: This a punk rock concert with a fierce kick, dominated by show-stopping performances and tunes. It plays against type for Disney, and that's a very good thing.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: This newfangled "Cruella" is too PC to skin pups for pelts. She's now the face of a more insidious evil: that of the self-involved, narcissistic soul-regression that evolves automatically just by being part of modern selfie culture. Fun though.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Too bad the movie is obsessed with giving every element in 101 Dalmatians an origin story, including the car.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: I was entertained throughout this entire film. The costume, set and makeup designs accompanied by wild performances by Emma Stone and Thompson make this worth the two plus hour film.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: The link to 101 Dalmatians is so tenuous. This is just a fun, crime, con-person romp.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Stone & Thompson's performances are great, costume design & cinematography are award worthy, & each moment is so much fun. One of the best live action Disney adaptations
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: This whole movie is as bold as the title character who has been elevated to near superhero status and the melodramatic performances are just as heightened.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: The fabulously fashionable workplace drama I never knew I needed... better than the recent live-action remakes of earlier Disney animations because it is merely inspired by the cartoon, not a recreation.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: Director Craig Gillespie and star Emma Stone have fashioned a wildly entertaining, enjoyable over-the-top success that managed to please my kids and me equally.
reviews.author: Christopher Schobert

reviews.text: There's so much to love here! I appreciated seeing Estella's (Cruella's) creativity shine and her bravery in facing hardship.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: 'Cruella' is a great pastime that takes a mythical character to completely take him to his turf instead of being a slave to the original work. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: An Anti-Disney Delight
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: Where is the Disney spark and magic? This is a rip-off, not an attempt at a classic.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Moving forward from early Dickensian dolor suiting an orphan to its "modern day," the quiet but swoony details of the film's look are comfortably in a school with work by the aces-of-aces designers like Anton Furst and Bo Welch. Eyeballs are duly popped.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: This movie is worth watching for how it looks and sounds and for Emma Thompson...
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: It's Solo: A Star Wars Story mixed with The Devil Wears Prada with a dash of Ocean's Eleven and a little A Hard Day's Night on the side.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: Punk rock and the fashion world collide in this admirable live action prequel. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Orlando Maldonado

reviews.text: The production design and costumes are impressive, and Stone gives her all. But that's it.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Cruella might as well be called The Joker Wears Prada.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: It's better to think of Craig Gillespie's Cruella as a riff than as a prequel--a variation on a theme rather than the puzzle-box predecessor to a beloved intellectual property.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Cruella is doing enough to be seductively fun and entertaining, at least for the first 90 minutes.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: ... an ill-conceived origin story for the iconic villainess, justifying her future malfeasance by positioning her as a rebellious mad genius trying to cope with oppressive circumstances.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Two Emmas for one low price! One is bipolar, the other bi-curious. After asking "why do this?" it's fun for the DALMATIAN UNIVERSE completists. Next: Cruella Marries the Hulk.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The movie is fun, stylish, and over the top (in mostly a good way), but it struggles to prove that it's more than a muddled cash grab.
reviews.author: Rebecca Long

reviews.text: It's classic Disney with a little bite - and something we needed to feel normal again.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: Disney finally creates a film that actually breathes new life into an earlier animated film, with a result that also stands on its own.
reviews.author: Bill Watters

reviews.text: At the end of the day, the most fun comes from seeing the two actresses not only bitterly duel, but also clearly enjoy their not exactly subtle roles. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: "Cruella" is a much better film than it needed to be ...the talents of the cast and the wonderful production design overcome the oddity of the retcon and the too-many-cooks flavor of the script.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Craig Gillespie splendidly directs a surprising film, very funny and with a fabulous rhythm. A very well told story, an excellent mise-en-scene and a fantastic soundtrack all led by the Emmas make Cruella a great movie. [Full review in spanish]
reviews.author: Alvaro Corujo

reviews.text: With a very unique style that sets it apart from previous Disney live action adaptations, Cruella is a fun ride full of surprises. The war between the two Emmas is the cherry on top. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Cruella competently stands shoulder to shoulder with a group of family films that don't feel like losing IQ points when it comes to entertaining kids.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: The duel of the Emmas is fun to watch... Jenny Bevan's costumes were absolutely phenomenal.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: Cruella sees two of the very best Emmas playing off against each other is a helter-skelter riotous romp of an origins story we didn't think we needed but now could not live without.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: Director Craig Gillespie infuses the story with a Roald Dahl sensibility, adding wonderfully nasty touches as well as terrific character elements that bring the story to life.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Cruella is often fun to watch, but its cavalier reversal of its core character cheapens the very idea of a corrective narrative. It takes a quintessential villain and nuances her character into oblivion.
reviews.author: Megan Garber

reviews.text: For the most part, Cruella manages to distract one from its origins and its purpose with a sense of style uncommon to these Disney Live-Action Remakes, and it, shockingly enough, isn't a horrible way to spend an evening.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: This becomes repetitive and one-note after you get past how deliciously wicked everyone is.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: It's devilishly entertaining. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: You either die a dog-killing villain or live long enough to be retconned into a girlboss antihero.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: ...more of a drama than an adventure, it's a strong and original film from the Disney brand...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Even though it's moving at breakneck speed, nothing seems to happen.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: The film really managed to capture the essence of a villain you can't help to love. Unlike Maleficent, the new optic of the antagonist works perfectly. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gabriela Meza

reviews.text: Very funny, and when we consider how easy it would've been to completely drop the ball, the fact that it's fun is seriously underrated...Thompson just sets the screen on fire.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Both lead actresses are fantastic, and Cruella is energetic and spunky...
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Despite all the issues, new audiences coming into Disney's Cruella without any expectations or without looking for movie timeline connections might have fun with it.
reviews.author: Shah Shahid

reviews.text: As someone who generally gets too angry about resurrected characters and origin stories, I found Cruella surprisingly energetic and happily twisted.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: Emma Stone fully embraces the role of Cruella De Vil and captures her rebellious attitude perfectly.
reviews.author: Megan Williams

reviews.text: It's a fabulous-darling air kiss of a movie, directed with the same winking brio Gillespie brought to I, Tonya, about the disgraced Olympic figure skater Tonya Harding.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Splendid as the performances are, the costumes by Mad Max: Fury Road Oscar winner Jenny Beavan (Stone has 47 changes in the film) are MVP here. Garments haven't told their own story like this since-well, another picture starring Stone, The Favourite.
reviews.author: Samuel R. Murrian

reviews.text: Although this film is not for me and struggles to hit 2/5, the 10-year-old I saw it with was so tickled by it and explicitly instructed me to note in this review that they give it a 4/5. So in the spirit of democracy, a 3/5 it is
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: Look after look after look by Jenny Bevan helped this film feel like a breeze. This movie also breezes by on the delicious acting decisions made by Thompson who revels in the villain-y of the Baroness.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: The performances are solid, the casting is great and the costumes -- well the costumes are gorgeous. But Cruella plays it too safe and never really finds its feet, let alone its voice.
reviews.author: Erik Kain

reviews.text: A chaos pairing of genre and tone? Or one that goes together like, say, a shock of black-and-white hair, parted severely in the middle to both startling and fashionable effect?
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: The movie acknowledges its Disney past but mostly succeeds in taking it to entertaining new levels.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It keeps everything family-friendly and age-appropriate, but for the most part it makes a convincing, visually lively effort to give the chain-smoking terror a convincing origin tale.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: It's an airplane movie just in time for us to maybe even go on an airplane again. The film is far too long, at two-plus hours, but there are much worse ways to spend around 140 minutes.
reviews.author: Emily Alford

reviews.text: Estella may not live up to the reputation of Cruella de Vil that preceded her, but if Emma Stone's take doesn't entertain you, nothing else will.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: An entertaining origin story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: But while Cruella is bursting with style and features two very arch, fun performances, it's never really able to avoid the spectre of all those spotted puppies and the image of a terrifying woman trying to kill those dogs to make a fur coat.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: It's in the film's favor that it moves away from the Disney formula. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Set against the punk-rock revolution in 1970s London, Cruella boasts a well-thought-out and -executed aesthetic that takes it up a notch.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Running at over two hours long, the prequel is a potpourri of classic rock songs and needle drops, with costume and set design by far the most interesting of its traits.
reviews.author: Rafaela Sales Ross

reviews.text: Cruella, the movie, is brash and brassy, stylish and wicked, and overall a thoroughly entertaining watch.
reviews.author: Josh Davis

reviews.text: It's hands-down Disney's best and punchiest prequel yet, one whose playful perils make for a deliciously rowdy ride.
reviews.author: Kate Stables

reviews.text: Some movies are meant to be fun and not taken so seriously. That's Disney's Cruella in a nutshell - enjoy the aesthetics and the madcap plot, not as a treatise on femininity and fashion, because that it is not.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: The Met Gala should be so lucky.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: Cruella is not as perfect as the seams Estella stitches, but there's something ever so charming about its strut.
reviews.author: Jenny Nulf

reviews.text: Stone's performance slips into high gear, reaching an entertainingly manic level. There's a crazed glint in her eye that is more than a match for Thompson's basilisk stare, and Gillespie's design department backs her up.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: A nearly idiosyncratic Disney retelling.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Thank goodness for Thompson. Her presence makes "Cruella" a Disneyfied version of "The Devil Wears Prada."
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: That Cruella is an atrocity with neither purpose nor soul shouldn't come as a surprise.
reviews.author: Angelica Jade Bastién

reviews.text: Stone is a joy: vampy, sneering and as eager to please as a dalmatian.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Despite gorgeous costuming, obligatory CGI displays, and relentless needle-drops in an overstuffed soundtrack, little in Cruella is earnest or inspired. It's eye-catching, but it's also incredibly empty.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Fashionably extravagant, twistedly tragic and deliriously hilarious, Cruella is wickedly entertaining.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: [Emma] Stone mixes Cruella with sweet vulnerability and stone cold insanity that is more reminiscent of a super hero character than a Disney one ... For once, it is better the de Vil you don't know rather than the one you grew up on.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Oscar-winner Emma Stone having the time of her life on screen with wicked laughs, sarcasm and award-worthy costumes. Yet it's Oscar-winner Emma Thompson as The Baroness who steals the show.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: With 2/3 being incredibly entertaining. mathematically I have to recommend it, though it would be nice to get a Disney Live-Action Remake that's enjoyable all the way through.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: There's not much of One Hundred and One Dalmatians author Dodie Smith's source material or its classic 1961 animated adaptation to be found inside Disney's Cruella, and I'm perfectly okay with that.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: A film doesn't need pretty costumes to be enjoyable, but it does need good storytelling-which is the missing ingredient in Cruella.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: The Emmas behind it are sublime. Emma Stone and Emma Thompson duke it out in oversize rolls they were born to play, and they're clearly having the time of their lives.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: With its sloppy storytelling and overall decimation of a beloved antagonist's definable maliciousness, Cruella is a shaggy, unkempt dog of a film that is a victim of its own fashion.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: It ultimately may not be reinventing the wheel, but Gillespie manages to breathe enough new life into Disney's live action remake formula with some stylistic tweaks and a darker, more grown up tone.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: This clogged-up mess doesn't need two Emmas. It needs an enema.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: (Emma) Stone and (Emma) Thompson are such gifted performers, (director Craig) Gillespie is content to let the two Oscar winners go after one another and eat each other alive.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: In telling viewers that Cruella is saddled with childhood traumas, too, it seems to think that two-plus over-stretched hours of 70s cosplay will suffice.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: It makes for a goofy watch even if it's not a memorable film.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Being an origin story of a woman who just wanted to turn a bunch of dogs into a coat means this side-steps the bloated stakes that often make Disney films feel try-hard
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: The re-imagined, color-blind, LBGTQ-friendly tale offers a schizophrenic approach to Cruella's inspired antics at fulfilling her designer dreams, but the comic book attitude just wants you to admire the scenery and laugh at the slapstick.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: The ground is laid, in the end, for the expected next chapter. I had enough fun this time around to give it a shot, too.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Clearly another brand extension product from Disney--the real draw here are the two leads.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: If this movie speaks to you, please don't speak to me.
reviews.author: Ian Simmons

reviews.text: Director Craig Gillespie ("I, Tonya") and five -- count 'em 5! -- credited screenwriters do dazzle with a few special moments, especially in areas of London-based extravaganza. Otherwise, theirs is a by-the-book procedure.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: The delights of this movie are the over-the-top performances of the Emmas Stone and Thompson, both overacting with a vengeance that it seems both enjoy.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: 'Cruella' is a film to behold rather than enjoy
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: Cruella is a tale of two Emmas, and one of the best of these Disney live action remakes thanks to the Oscar winning actresses.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Even if it answers questions about Cruella de Vil that nobody ever really had, this runway is all slay, all day. This is the glam slam villain jam we didn't know we needed.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: Cruella is exhilarating to witness in its unruly attitude. With a peppy soundtrack, enjoyably pantomime acting from both Stone and Thompson, a refreshingly mean streak and the stylistic excess through its production; it is delectably good fun.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: An absolutely delicious, visually sumptuous treat...a distinctly adult-oriented lark with a decidedly dark edge and lots of Goth costuming, magnificent sets, splashy camerawork and playful period detail, with special attention paid to men's hairstyles.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: It's fun to play the villain and [Emma] Stone definitely has a blast.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: When it counts, Craig Gillespie's blockbuster proves delicious.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: "From the very beginning I've always made a statement," Cruella announces at the outset in voice-over. Very true, and the movie that bears her name makes statements of its own - a lot of them. It just can't decide which ones matter
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: At the end of the day, Cruella may have some serious mother issues, but she isn't really cruel.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: It's just unfortunate that the muscular legacy of Cruella should, for now, end like this. Without a hint of cruelty at all.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: A heist, a necklace, a birth certificate and the Baroness's pet Dalmatians are all rather crowbarred into the narrative, but it's good energetic fun, sumptuous to look at, and perfect half-term fodder...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Beavan's costumes are dazzling throughout, including Cruella's glittering red dress at the Baroness's gala. But when the costumes overwhelm the characters and story, there's something hollow at the film's centre.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Clothes to die for, a script that needed more life.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: At two-plus hours, "Cruella" could use a few trims. But as a mood board, it's a smashing success.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: As much of a good time as Cruella is, it's still a shiny piece of IP from Disney.
reviews.author: Katey Stoetzel

reviews.text: It never completely works, although the cast is trying exceptionally hard.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: A fantastically beautiful piece, and very interesting as well.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: A movie that knows precisely when to pull the levers of familiarity and when to whirl off into some unexpected realm of dark whimsy.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: The endless hit parade of tunes ends up a huge distraction. And, despite being based on an animated movie, Cruella is far too dark and too long for youngsters. It could have used a 45-mniute edit.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Does Cruella really explain how a woman was born brilliant, bad, and a little bit mad? Not really. But if you're looking to spend a little over two hours in a Devil Wears Prada-like dance between two quite fabulous Emmas, then step right up.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: This movie is probably one of the better prequel films from the "House of Mouse", but at the same time it is stuck in the constraints of being a Disney movie.
reviews.author: Jamal Grootboom

reviews.text: Even with reservations, there's fun to be had in large portions here, and craft on display to marvel at.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Emma and Emma are delightful nemeses, both of them archly sarcastic in dueling posh accents.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: Cruella shines as quite possibly one of the strongest new-era live-action Disney films.
reviews.author: Mia Johnson

reviews.text: A solid film with a slightly sinister sensibility that's going to please Disney fans.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: It's all so much sugary ear- and eye-candy, without any real nutritional narrative underpinning. As such, the film wears out its welcome well before its exhaustive runtime is through.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Cruella is surprisingly fun, high-energy, creative romp that spills outside the boundaries of expectations for its premise.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: Gird your expectations a little and enjoy.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Parents should note the PG-13 rating onCruella,which is earned through a series of nightmarish scenes involving death, abandonment, and revenge. After putting us through the wringer,Cruellaleaves us with an inexcusably weak punchline and postscript.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: You don't always need a backstory for a popular big-screen villain... but it's impressive just how well they pulled this one off.
reviews.author: Kevin Brackett

reviews.text: It makes for jarring yet engaging viewing; I liked this better than I thought I would.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: This movie surprised me... It's a gorgeous-looking movie.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Despite some fun moments + stunning costumes, at 2 hr 14 minutes it's overlong and lacks a biting sense of humor that prevents it from being a rollicking good time.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Cruella is a fairly enjoyable spectacle, but, like Maleficent, it shrinks its title character a bit.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: While no classic, it's hard to resist "Cruella's" fashionable charms.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: [Cruella is] a fun, fashion fueled fantasy that is ultimately weighed down by its connection to the Disney franchise.
reviews.author: Rain Jokinen

reviews.text: Forget about the plot: ask your heroine to pose in splendiferous outfits; crank up the Stones, the Zombies, the Clash, or Doris Day; and, woof, there's your movie.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: A Dickensian fantasia and near musical with a soundtrack of '60s and '70s classics and a signature role for Emma Stone.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Watching the two Emmas deliciously trade barbs and play up their crackling rivalry is worth the ticket price.
reviews.author: Jeanmarie Tan

reviews.text: The performances are generally good, the production and fashion designs are top-notch, and the flick contains a great soundtrack of old popular tunes.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Though not exactly the most original film, Cruella is a fun and fashionable watch. The Emmas are splendid, dahling, and I would gladly spend hours watching them duke it out.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: This dark origin story of evil fashionista, Cruella de Vil, actually unleashes dueling Emmas in 70's London with a parade of outfits to kill for. Bold and wonderfully anti-Disney in style.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: ... Disney's best live-action attempt to date reimagining their own iconic animation... the familiar beats of a superhero origin story... built upon Stone's raw power and killer fashion...
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Mediocre mishmash of a movie.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Think of it as The Devil Wears Prada, if both the monster mentor and the put-upon employee were sociopathic and possibly murderous. When two formidable Emmas let fly, everyone else stands back.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: Paul Walter Hauser delivering a terrible cockney accent should bring joy, but in Cruella it merely elicits a resigned shrug.
reviews.author: Cathy Brennan

reviews.text: Two Oscar-winning Emmas-Stone and Thompson-are dressed to wow and deliver much to enjoy in this beautifully crafted fluffball, but the end result is a decorative distraction that never runs the risks it promises.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Cruella plays like the result of an endless script conference that generated only partial answers to the questions being asked.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: It's probably a good thing Cruella no longer wants garments PETA would hate. But it's too bad she's not more fun.
reviews.author: Dan Lybarger

reviews.text: A few things keep it from being perfect, but overall it's a good prequel. (And that's not something you can say about too many prequels.)
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Talky and relatively quick on its feet, ably cast with great supporting actors (Mark Strong, among them) and, of course, a few cute dogs.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Though the story may not entirely hold up as a villain origin or even as a retelling of a classic, there's enough charisma and guts to Cruella to make it an entertaining endeavor that's well worth the price of admission.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: "Cruella" won't be to everyone's taste, but to borrow from the original song, if Stone and Thompson squaring off doesn't entertain you at least a little, no evil thing will.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: [A] hollow exercise in corporate synergy that is all the worse thanks to its mistaken belief that it has some kind of rebellious, mold-breaking spirit that it simply does not possess.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: As sheer spectacle overlaying a sly rebuke to modern feminist values, it pays off.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: The picture is slick but dull, glitzy but witless, expensively boring.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Cruella instructs Millennials that their own psychosis is excusable, admirable, and fun.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: It's worth checking out, though it's unlikely to be anyone's repeat favorite.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: An unremarkable (although certainly not awful) family film (with a PG-13 rating) that lacks a compelling reason to exist.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Enjoy "Cruella" as a decadent and exhilarating standalone, daaaarling.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: It's a lifeless slog, and, with a running time of 134 minutes, a cruelly elongated one.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Cruella had some memorable moments, however, it continues the trend of Disney's live-action movies not coming close to the magic that is captured in their animated counterparts.
reviews.author: Britany Murphy

reviews.text: Cruella gets a punk rock glam infusion
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: It also has more than a whiff of Jekyll & Hyde to it, and the film's pleasures are many. Alas, so are its problems. This reboot is, to coin a term, spotty.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: A delightfully twisted origin story for the Disney villain. Emma Stone is an electric lead, but it's Joel Fry and Paul Walter Hauser who deliver more than expected - turning Cruella's bumbling henchmen into fully realized characters with loads of heart.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Stone, sporting a rascally glint in her eye as Cruella plots her moves, and Thompson, whose baroness, suggesting a meaner version of Meryl Streep's Devil Wears Prada character, all hauteur and ruthlessness, are a kick to watch.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: With such a rich sandbox to play in, and so much acting talent - an intergenerational Emma versus Emma - it's odd that Cruella feels so lacking in personality, never locating that spark of genuine weirdness that might have made it land as a classic.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: It's fun, a bit funky, certainly fresh (check out the soundtrack) and, yes, it works fabulously.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Villain origin story is Mean Girl vs. Mean Girl, and nastiness is not only encouraged and played for laughs, but rewarded. Please take PG-13 seriously. Stars are designers.
reviews.author: Nora Lee Mandel

reviews.text: Its daringness to be character-driven and different (in a Tim Burton/Batman kind of way) isn't so black and white. It's killer fun!
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: [Emma Stone and Emma Thompson] bring that fun to the forefront, and all that fun has to do with the characters interacting... What hobbles this movie [is that the filmmakers] try to crush it into this box that is "Disney villain origin story."
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Stone and Thompson are both talented actresses who play their cartoonish characters to the hilt, but they can't defeat the basic problem with the script: it wants us to sympathize with a woman who we know will someday want to kill puppies.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: You don't need to be [a fan of 101 Dalmatians] to enjoy it. If anything, Cruella could hold as a stand-alone for anyone who simply enjoys high fashion, bold characters, fast plots and, well, adorable dogs.
reviews.author: Janice Rodrigues

reviews.text: What's black, white and wittily wicked fun all over?
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: Cruella is clearly not without its flaws, but to borrow a phrase from Tim Gunn, they made it work.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Stone and Thompson bite deep into their roles and both succeed -- especially Thompson -- but the kitschy snazziness of caricature is mostly what registers.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: It's all in good fun, for the most part.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: The two Emmas are superb, and the edginess of the story is a nice deviation from what I expected.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: [T]he Cruella of Cruella -- what we're meant to think about her and about who she'll become -- remains a bit too much of an open-ended question.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: I had rather modest expectations for Cruella. They were far surpassed.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Wickedly stylish and an absolute gas, it's essentially a fashion film, full of immaculate gowns and unabashed showmanship.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Like a designer fond of hitting vintage shops for inspiration, "Cruella" does take something old and reworks it into something that feels fresh and new.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Even though his film is dragged down by its criminally long runtime and weirdly sympathetic sob story, Cruella is a delightful romp full of fashionable heists and over-the-top theatrics.
reviews.author: Petrana Radulovic

reviews.text: All this wicked cynicism aside, 'Cruella' actually does find a measure of sweetness and humanity, perhaps largely thanks to the casting of Emma Stone.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: In a sure sign there were script issues, six writers are credited and none can decide what to do with their main character.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: The show belongs to Stone, who is a bracing presence from the moment she first appears, adjusting her red wig in a mirror.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: A sleek and stylish dive into the titular character's humble beginnings.
reviews.author: Melody McCune

reviews.text: As it is, Cruella is a mostly good time and always a terrific spectacle.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: A twisted tale for a cynical time. Where mean is queen, as feminism finds itself, following hopeful and inspiring origins in the late last century, at the crossroads of combo cancel culture and right wing onslaught - and endangered species irrelevance.
reviews.author: Prairie Miller

reviews.text: They had great music, really awesome fashion, a lot of fun reveal moments... Emma Stone and Emma Thompson had this great dynamic together.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: A great excuse for its two leading actresses Emma Stone and Emma Thompson, to face off, both divine, but the latter probably in the best performance of her career. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea G. Bermejo

reviews.text: A misconceived prequel that's too archly artificial for kids, too witlessly juvenile for adults, and too tedious for viewers of any age.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Everyone involved with Cruella appears to have taken great care in making sure it was higher quality than the typical Disney live-action film, and it shows.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Much like the sets, costumes, and performances in Cruella, everything about Craig Gillespie's film is big. The inspiration of a Disney-style version of The Devil Wears Prada is blatant, but it's done with spectacular, invigorating results.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: As of this writing, the good stuff outweighs the bad. Ask me tomorrow, and I might say the opposite.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: A mile wide and an inch deep.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Cruella somehow manages to fail to engage with just about any population it's aiming to please.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Cruella is a visually bold and fiendishly fun crime romp featuring a fantastic dynamic between Emma Stone and Emma Thompson.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: Exhaustingly over-directed...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: So how does one make a woman famously described as evil incarnate the protagonist of her own story? ... I still don't know.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: Cruella has lots going for it. Great costume design, a rippin' soundtrack and arch attitude, but by the time the end credits roll, it is all about the dueling Emmas, Stone and Thompson.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Cruella's visuals are intricate, and intriguing inviting the audience to come inside and explore.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Rather than fall back on formula, Cruella uses its animated and live action predecessors as a mere launch pad for something different and dazzlingly original.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Wickedly entertaining! It's got cool fashion, an awesome soundtrack and, most importantly, a great sense of humor. Ends up elevating Disney's classic villain. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: One of the studio's best live-action adaptations yet.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: ...this twist on the Dodie Smith novel is punk rock meets The Devil Wears Prada, as if it was imagined by Batman's Tim Burton.
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: I've seen far worse Disney recycling jobs, which doesn't make "Cruella" any more than it is: a "Joker" for jaded Disney princess fans everywhere.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Overall, Cruella is definitely one of the better live-action remakes that Disney has put out.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: It's one of the best triumph-of-evil movies to come along in years - not quite as masterful as "The Godfather Part II," perhaps, but certainly miles above "Joker" or "Birds of Prey."
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Less a prequel and more a reimagining ... expressive, fun and enjoyable.
reviews.author: Thomas Caldwell

reviews.text: Fresh-faced Grand Guignol.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Cruella surprises with a energetic story of heist, revenge and wickedness; a bombastic 70's inspired soundtrack and Emma Stone going ALL-IN. Like the kids say: "she understood the assignment". [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Featuring some breathtaking costume designs and a soundtrack that keeps up with the script's lavish personality, Cruella is a welcome return to the good, dark, bold filmmaking that we haven't seen in a long time from Disney.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: The film drags on...and on...and on...seemingly starting a new plot line every half hour or so.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: Wickedly funny, witty, and full of pizzazz. It's a thrilling comedy and fascinating psychological drama with stellar performances by Emma Stone and Emma Thompson.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Emma Stone is giving Harley Quinn/Miranda Priestly Realness as Cruella/. Emma Thompson wears evil well and the production design on this film from the soundtrack to costumes is insanely exquisite
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: As for Thompson, she's having a grand time, her lines dripping with so much disdain, her co-stars likely had to be dried off after each scene.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Too much of "The Devil Wears Prada" and a script that goes on for too long, but enough laughs courtesy of Ms. Thompson and a surprisingly nuanced performance by Ms. Stone make it an overall acceptable villain origin story
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: The movie is not very good but there's a lot to look at and listen to and much of it is fun to watch.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: ...the bespoke balance of light and darkness is rocked with such utmost confidence and poise that it looks absolutely fabulous.
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: Disney is anything but punk. But for just a few moments, Cruella lets them pretend they are.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: It's unclear if Disney is rewriting history to change its villain or if the studio's leaving something open for a potential sequel.
reviews.author: Kirsten Acuna

reviews.text: Swaying between outlandish and expected, the movie ultimately feels like a clumsy compromise. Still, with grimy whimsy, crackling leading ladies, imaginative twists, and plenty of eye-popping spectacle, Cruella is a hell of a good time.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Cruella is a pompous spectacle with a punk rock vibe. Every aspect of Disney's origins story is outrageous but so much fun to revel in. The film is gorgeous to look at.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: Emma Thompson arrives and the whole film comes to life. Her evil fashion maven, The Baroness, feels like a real old-school Disney villain; glamorous, arch, and gleefully evil.
reviews.author: Amelia Berry

reviews.text: See Cruella for the fun performances and the fashion.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Emma Stone dazzles in Cruella. A classic cartoon villainess gets an ultra hip, haute punk couture origin story.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: It all collapses into a messy swamp of content, which is exactly the capitalist nuclear soup that gives rise to a movie like Cruella.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: The good news is that Cruella...is a surprisingly enjoyable confection that feels on par quality-wise with Disney's live-action remakes of Cinderella and Beauty & The Beast
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: The movie refuses to go dark enough to make Cruella an all-out villain, thus offering a tepid and disappointing origin story that fails to ignite any passions.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Cruella is a dog with a big bark and no teeth to back up its snarl.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: As if an unspoken, but important, character in the film, Jenny Beavan's costume designs are sensational.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: Deliberately leaps into the stupidest possible version of its premise within the first 10 minutes, then makes a performance-of rebuilding itself [as] a revenge story of "Girl Boss vs Girl Boss But-Being-Performatively-Ironic-About-It"
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: Despite the character's limitations, Gillespie's dizzyingly manic aesthetic makes for a head-rush of a ride, as we trip the light fantastic through a grungy glam-goth take on '70s London.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: When I say it has something for everyone I'm not being sarcastic, though I'm also not being entirely complimentary.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Gorgeous costumes, sumptuous sets and even spot-on acting can't make up for a story that makes little sense -- and is borderline violent.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: CRUELLA is a mean-spirited, overly-long, predictable and unfunny film. Other than that, it does have some redeeming qualities.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: It's like Gillespie and his team of writers couldn't figure out how to make their protagonist evil while keeping the audience on side, so settled for leaving her as a slightly inconsiderate antihero.
reviews.author: Mark Cassidy

reviews.text: In this 'battle of the villains' origin story, Cruella [the film] can be a little overstuffed and filled with inconsistencies, but the dynamic duo of Emma Stone and Emma Thompson (as well as top-notch costume design) elevate this sometimes tedious movie.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: It needed to have gone further in its ghoulishness (it's already terribly close to a work by Tim Burton) or dialed it back to the realm of over-the-top goofiness.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: This film takes the audience on twists and turns leading to an unexpected place. But a place where it is quite obvious there will be sequels to spawn from Cruella's character. I highly recommend this film.
reviews.author: Katrina Olson

reviews.text: Emma Stone is so great in Cruella... There's a scene where she really knocks it out of the park, and I think she deserves to be nominated for an award for that performance.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: Stone's transition from wide-eyed innocent to the beastly Cruella is not exactly subtle, but she's still fun to watch in pantomime mode.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Deviously evil, live-action origin story - it's wonderfully wicked and commendable for its LGBTQ+ representation.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The production defangs one of Disney's great baddies, creating a bloated psychological study that's not interesting. And it's short 98 dalmatians.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Villain apologetics just don't work, especially when lined up with their bad actions. But even with this, Cruella is just a good film. It's beautifully made...
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Gillespie and company spin a devilishly alluring crowdpleaser despite some foundational issues.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Stone and Thompson's performances and the costume designs offer tasty ingredients, but it felt more like a calculated effort to establish a franchise few wanted.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: This is a Disney franchise movie about spring and fall collections, with an anti-hero weaponizing haute couture designs, which are so stunning and elaborate they are their own set pieces.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: The visuals were stunning, the dialogue was on point, and the costume design was ridiculously charming and edgy. This film and these characters were made for this cast.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: A Disney-fied poduct that isn't as dark or gritty as it believes itself to be
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: The script makes sturdy bones for the costumes, scene-stealing of course, their mad dazzle matched by the set pieces.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Cruella is glossy enough to catch your eye, but there's nothing under that sheen that sticks with you.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Sinisterly superb, this is a well-crafted, phenomenally acted, artistically drenched triumph that's a whole lot more responsible than most other villain-as-main-character films.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Disney's Cruella is an unexpected joy, albeit an overlong one. Bonus: good dogs.
reviews.author: Amelia Emberwing

reviews.text: Gillespie helms a stunning showcase of talent that culminates in a striking feature, but it's narratively hollow and toothless.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: Like Cruella's occasionally piebald hair, it's very much a movie of two halves: fun to look at, if a little fleeting.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Can't we just have our villains? For a company that has become legendary for Disney-fying stories that originally had more edge, Cruella might be their most Disney-fied effort to date.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: A movie that tries so hard to be stylish it accomplishes only the impression of style, the sense that this is supposed to be a feast for the eyes, while making little effort to prevent the viewer's lids from closing when the plot bores them to sleep.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: A disjointed mess... ultimately, the whole thing just fell flat for me.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The most stylish and extravagant Disney live-action re-imagining to date! (With) unique charm and flair... wicked style, bombastic fun and sickly twisted humor. Emma Stone is absolutely devilish and delivers the powerhouse performance of her career.
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: The film is flawed, but when it's good it's SO good! Both Emmas are absolutely fabulous, and the movie screams for a sequel. A lot of fun & very clever. Needs a new director.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Sure, she could kill them with kindness and be the change she wishes to see in the world, but her name is Cruella, not Gandhi.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Cruella is the movie version of fast fashion - it looks good but the substance isn't there. The magic is in watching Stone and Thompson go tête-à-tête to The Stooges in punk-haute couture, while the rest of the movie sort of exists in the background.
reviews.author: Gabriella Geisinger

reviews.text: Stylish, fresh and wickedly anarchic.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: A lot worse than it thinks it is.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: A fierce and fiesty central performance from Emma Stone is matched by a creatively cruel turn from Emma Thompson. The real star here is the production design and the costumes. A great fun film, with a wicked look.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: Cruella's a crime caper with canines, couture, and a crazy collection of colorful characters.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: [I]n these [fashion show interrupting] scenes, DP Nicolas Karakatsanis is given more creative freedom to showcase the avant-garde fashions, giving Cruella a cinematic quality not found in most of the studio's recent output.
reviews.author: Marshall Estes

reviews.text: The Emmas! The Fashion! The Music! Cruella is a vibrant, fun, cinematic triumph and the best live-action Disney film.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Emma Stone's version of the character bears no resemblance to de Vil other than a striking haircut, but there's still some fun to be had with this glitzy, pop art origin story
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: One of the better live-action Disney efforts, as the film has a real pulse and sense of style to give it something extra.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: It has fun with the dastardly origin story, embedding itself amid the fashionable rebels of 1970s London and generally going big any way it can.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Cruella is a darker, smarter, and more stylistic film than anticipated. While it may not appeal to the younger crowd, there is a lot to appreciate here.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Not only is Cruella a fashion designer's paradise, it's an extravagant and entertaining film that also challenges us to look at people in shades of gray.
reviews.author: Shannon McGrew

reviews.text: Emma Stone shines in Cruella, which also doubles as one of Disney's best live-action retreads of their animated classics yet.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: Cruella has the pulsating energy of a rock concert and is the best Disney live-action yet.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: The film might have faltered but for the irresistible tête-à-tête at its core.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The overwritten slog that is "Cruella" never gives a reason for its existence. Seriously, who wanted this movie?
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Viewers who think of this less as a reboot of Dodie Harris' memorable monster and more as a Disney spin on Derek Jarman's Jubilee for gay 8-year-olds will find "Cruella" to be flashy fun, even at a slightly bloated two-hours-plus running time.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Disney doesn't usually do sympathy for the devil (or De Vil, as it were), but somehow, it works.
reviews.author: Aly Caviness

reviews.text: Stylish, calculating and beautiful with a pair of perfectly-pitched performances from its two leads, Cruella is an apt reflection of the life its heroine wants to lead but may be a decade too late in getting there.
reviews.author: Joshua Starnes

reviews.text: The film's overall punk vibe is what truly sets it apart from anything else Disney has ever made.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: Outlandishly stylish and fiendishly clever, 'Cruella' upends expectations to demonstrate that origin stories can be roundly entertaining.
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: Is it long? Yes, by about 30 minutes, but it's still good fun.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Dress porn doesn't even begin to describe the sartorial eye candy on display here, and Stone's magnetic performance sells it completely.
reviews.author: Rosie Fletcher

reviews.text: The Dalmatian-obsessed fashionista's backstory might not have been something we needed, but it sure is an unexpected, campy treat.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: The whole effect is over the top and satisfyingly wacky. Poor Estella, she's the Catwoman of the Disney universe. And she's not done, not by a long shot.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: A wicked, camp surprise that has no right to be as delicious as it is.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: It's hard for one to get on board with feeling empathy for Cruella when we know she will one day be terrorizing animals.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: This is pure Disney razzle-dazzle, every bit as fanciful as the story its based on.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: There are so many things right about Disney's latest villainous spin on the origin story it's a shame that one thing that is very, very wrong indeed casts a shadow over the proceedings.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The Emmas' devilish performances make it wicked good fun! Just enough evil without going overboard for Disney's fanbase. But why is it so long?
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: A movie that flinches from its own premise, even as it looks great doing it.
reviews.author: Matt Zoller Seitz

reviews.text: The film is so intent on redeeming the character it neuters Stone's performance, transforming what should have been the glorious emergence of her wicked side into a misjudged parable...
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Cruella is an eclectically mischievous rollercoaster, at once an extravagant blockbuster and worthwhile character study
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Brazenly bold and expertly woven, Cruella excels on multiple fronts - prime being its dark humor and aesthetics, and a deliciously sublime Emma Stone.
reviews.author: Debopriyaa Dutta

reviews.text: The film takes the idea of a Cruella de Vil origin story so deathly seriously that it ends up being funny when it's not trying to be.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: Achieves the dubious feat of being tedious, transgressive, chaotic and inert at the same time.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: While there's energy and edge to the picture, "Cruella" feels stitched together from different influences in order to justify a rather blatant attempt to renew interest in a moribund property.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Cruella isn't offensive in any way, but you'll be left wondering what was the point.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: With killer looks, propulsive filmmaking, and stellar turns from Emmas Stone and Thompson, Cruella is a Spring/Summer '21 treat.
reviews.author: Ben Travis

reviews.text: As remakes and spin-offs go, this one's barking up the right tree.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: A movie as shiny and hectic as Cruella: a heady exercise in style and scenery-chewing whose high-gloss chaos seems designed less for cohesive storytelling or world-building than for looking super-cool in previews.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: In every lull in the film I found myself trying to figure out why exactly Cruella exists, entertaining as it is.
reviews.author: Alex Cranz

reviews.text: If this movie DOESN'T win Academy Awards for best makeup and hairstyling and best costume design, I can't wait to see what tops it.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: If you love fashion, devilish fun, and watching women be unapologetically bad, Cruella is a must-see.
reviews.author: Jamie Jirak

reviews.text: They're the villains that we hate. Don't make them into the heroes that we love.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: The two Emmas slay in their respective performances while Gillespie does an incredible job crafting an epic '70s period piece that relishes in both upscale and punk fashion.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: When she's playing Cruella, Stone is definitely in charge. It's a bravura performance, filled with a crackling energy that never spills over into parody. That's what saves it.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: "Cruella" feels like a wildly imaginative superhero movie, but with fashion instead of superpowers.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Surface pleasures go a long way toward concealing the film's blemishes...
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: Cruella threatens us with a good time and delivers most fabulously.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Stone seethes, stews and schemes with aplomb. And Thompson gives her truly vile villainess plenty of oomph, taking a perfectionist's care with her delivery.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: From its powerful LGBTQ messages to its insane fashion, this is precisely the campy film I want to see from Disney. Have fun, embrace the strange...and Cruella does that.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: With a wickedly impressive fashion sense, an electric retro soundtrack and its sinfully entertaining title character, "Cruella" is the coolest Disney film in forever.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: If you ask whether it's enough to be entertaining, however, the answer changes to the affirmative. It flaunts its refusal to know what subtlety means.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: The battle of the Emmas is as hard to resist on-screen as it must have been on paper, even if it's not exactly a fair fight.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Perhaps the biggest question of Cruella is not how she got the way she got, but who this movie is for.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: One of the most vivaciously deviant Disney properties to ever come flying out of the movie mousehole.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: It's the first time in the last decade that one of Disney's reimaginings feels fresh and exciting.
reviews.author: Brandon Katz

reviews.text: Deliciously devilish, wonderfully wicked, sensational perfection that's a must-see on the big screen.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: It doesn't really succeed on the prequel front, but Cruella still stands on its own as an energetic, entertaining, and atypical comedy.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: Stone is perfect casting here, managing to give more than one dimension to the young Cruella and keeping us curious as to how she eventually will inhabit the all-out villainy of the evil presence she inhabited in the previous Disney outings.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: This is not your kid's Cruella. And that is a very good thing.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: What Cruella lacks in script... it makes up for in sheer visual punch, with costume designer Jenny Beavan's exquisitely detailed gowns especially enriching the angsty, sinister universe the film conjures.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

reviews.text: One of the best Disney live-action adaptations to date, 'Cruella' proves the studio can do an origin story without muddying the reputation and legacy of one of its beloved icons.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Like all villains, Cruella just wants to be understood. As spotty as her origin story may be, it accomplishes that in style.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: At its core, Cruella is really just the chewed-up leftovers of other popular fare.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: Draping a polka-dot pelt over The Devil Wears Prada, even those squarely in Cruella's campy camp might not find its stylish hate couture a perfect fit.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: The world was not clamoring for an origin story about the "101 Dalmatians" villain, Cruella de Vil, and the movie doesn't justify making one.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: After a few meaningful surprises in its opening scenes, most of Cruella is painfully predictable.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: The film's outward liveliness can't mask the inner inertia it has as just another lifeless product assembled in a factory.
reviews.author: Pat Brown

reviews.text: Cruella delivers Disney's best live-action film yet, due to bold direction, dazzling costumes, and striking performances from Emma Stone and Emma Thompson.
reviews.author: Sharronda Williams

reviews.text: "Cruella" proves ingeniously creative in its reimagining of the underlying IP.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: The biggest surprise of 2021, Cruella is a bold, striking, and visually stunning delight featuring a fierce, transformative performance from Emma Stone that sees her make Cruella de Vil entirely her own. A must-see.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: It's overlong, and perhaps tries to be too many different things at once, but Cruella can still be counted as one of the better live-action Disney films to date.
reviews.author: Patrick Cremona

reviews.text: Chaos, mayhem, and wickedness have always been at the core of Cruella de Vil's appeal, and when those elements take center stage, the film is quite fun - I just wish it had spent less time focusing on wearisome backstory and more time reviling in devilry.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Cruella is often infectiously entertaining despite its faults, and reframing Cruella de Vil as a devious stunt queen, at least for the briefest sparkle of a few moments, feels sublime.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: A visually stunning journey into one of Disney's darkest villains, in which Emma Stone absolutely crushes the role. The costumes, the sets, and the soundtrack are all PERFECT.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Kindly step back and make way for a sensational couple of Emmas: Stone and Thompson. Together, they are the highly strung dysfunctional double-act that post-lockdown cinema didn't know it needed.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Both Stone and Thompson are clearly having the time of their lives chewing the scenery and taking swipes at each other - with Stone's snide derision matching Thompson's haughty high maintenance at every turn.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Unlike Maleficent, which is less beholden to the past as it shifts Sleeping Beauty's villain into a truly sympathetic character, Cruella comes across more as a punk poser, a faux white hat whose potential heroism is overshadowed by her future.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: In what might be the mouse house's riskiest adaptation yet, a 1970s steampunk PG13 revenge caper set in the "101 Dalmation" universe, "Cruella" marks a creative and stylish rebound from the likes of two dreary "Maleficent" flicks.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Emma Thompson will most likely require some amount of reconstructive surgery on her jaw from the amount of scenery she chew throughout this movie.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Jenny Beavan's costumes are nothing short of spectacular, the real showstopper, but while style can be substance, Cruella lacks a filmmaker behind the camera that knows how to make it so. [Full Review in Spanish]

synopsis: Academy Award (R) winner Emma Stone ("La La Land") stars in Disney's "Cruella," an all-new live-action feature film about the rebellious early days of one of cinemas most notorious - and notoriously fashionable - villains, the legendary Cruella de Vil. "Cruella," which is set in 1970s London amidst the punk rock revolution, follows a young grifter named Estella, a clever and creative girl determined to make a name for herself with her designs. She befriends a pair of young thieves who appreciate her appetite for mischief, and together they are able to build a life for themselves on the London streets. One day, Estella's flair for fashion catches the eye of the Baroness von Hellman, a fashion legend who is devastatingly chic and terrifyingly haute, played by two-time Oscar (R) winner Emma Thompson ("Howards End," "Sense & Sensibility"). But their relationship sets in motion a course of events and revelations that will cause Estella to embrace her wicked side and become the raucous, fashionable and revenge-bent Cruella.
